html-viewer.assumptionNote: The preview runs in a sandboxed iframe: scripts, forms, and plugins are blocked for safety.
benefits: Preview HTML instantly without saving files or running a server.
Sandboxed iframe keeps even untrusted snippets from running scripts.
Auto-render updates the preview as you type; manual mode renders on demand.
Light and dark preview backgrounds test both color schemes.
Character and line counts help with snippet size limits.

faqs.a: Paste your HTML into the editor. With auto-render on, the preview updates as you type. Turn auto-render off for large documents and press Render when ready.
faqs.q: How do I preview my HTML?

faqs.a: The iframe uses sandbox="" with no allow-scripts, so JavaScript cannot run inside the preview. This keeps the tool safe even with HTML you did not write yourself.
faqs.q: Is it safe to preview HTML from untrusted sources?

faqs.a: No. Scripts are intentionally blocked by the sandbox. The viewer is for markup and styling; use your browser's devtools or a local server to test JavaScript.
faqs.q: Why does my JavaScript not run in the preview?

faqs.a: The sandbox also blocks form submission, popups, and plugins. If your snippet needs those, test it in a real page instead.
faqs.q: Why does my form not submit in the preview?

faqs.a: Yes. The srcdoc attribute carries the full document, so <style> blocks and inline styles render exactly like a saved file would.
faqs.q: Does CSS in a <style> tag work?

faqs.a: The editor caps input at 200,000 characters to keep the tab responsive. For larger files, save them locally and open them in the browser.

html-viewer.formula:
<iframe
  srcdoc="<your HTML>"
  sandbox=""
  title="Preview">
</iframe>

sandbox="" blocks: scripts, forms,
plugins, popups, same-origin access.
howTo: Paste raw HTML into the editor box.
Keep auto-render on for live updates, or turn it off for big files.
Switch the preview background between light and dark.
Press Render in manual mode to update the preview.
Use the character count to stay within snippet limits.
keyFacts: The srcdoc attribute lets an iframe render HTML directly from a string.
sandbox="" blocks scripts, forms, popups, and plugins inside the frame.
External stylesheets and images load only if the URLs are reachable.
The preview renders exactly what a browser would show for the markup.
Input is capped at 200,000 characters to protect performance.
html-viewer.keywords: html viewer, html preview online, render html, html live preview, test html snippet

labels.errorTooLong: Input exceeds 200,000 characters and was trimmed.

limitations: JavaScript never runs in the preview — the sandbox blocks scripts.
Forms cannot submit and popups cannot open inside the frame.
External resources need network access and valid URLs.
Very large documents may render slowly on low-end devices.
